CYTOGENETICS LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted location] Medical Center
Department of Clinical Genetics

PATIENT INFORMATION
Patient Name: [redacted name]
Date of Birth: [redacted date]
Medical Record Number: [redacted ID]
Specimen Type: Placental tissue (uncultured)
Date Collected: [redacted date]
Date Received: [redacted date]
Date Reported: [redacted date]

CLINICAL INDICATION
Analysis of fetal tissue post-miscarriage

TEST PERFORMED
Quantitative Fluorescence Polymerase Chain Reaction (QF-PCR)
Analysis of uncultured placental material using microsatellite markers for chromosomes 13, 14, 15, 16, 18, 21, 22, X and Y

METHODOLOGY
DNA was extracted from uncultured placental tissue. QF-PCR analysis was performed using a panel of short tandem repeat (STR) markers specific for chromosomes 13, 14, 15, 16, 18, 21, 22, X and Y. Peak area ratios were calculated for informative markers to assess chromosome copy number. The presence of Y-specific sequences was evaluated using amelogenin and SRY markers.

RESULTS

Chromosome 16: ABNORMAL - Trisomy 16
- D16S539: 1:1:1 triallelic pattern
- D16S3018: 2:1 diallelic pattern (peak ratio 2.1:1)
- D16S3031: 1:1:1 triallelic pattern
- D16S3024: 2:1 diallelic pattern (peak ratio 1.9:1)
- D16S3017: 1:1:1 triallelic pattern
- D16S3121: 2:1 diallelic pattern (peak ratio 2.0:1)
- D16S3040: 1:1:1 triallelic pattern
Conclusion: Seven informative markers confirm trisomy 16

Sex Chromosomes: ABNORMAL - Monosomy X (45,X)
- AMELX/Y: Single X peak, no Y peak detected
- SRY: Absent
- DXS6809: Single allele
- DXS6807: Single allele
- XHPRT: Single allele
- DXS8377: Single allele
Conclusion: Single X chromosome with no Y-specific sequences detected, consistent with Turner syndrome (45,X)

Chromosome 13: Normal disomic pattern
- All informative markers show expected 1:1 or single allele patterns

Chromosome 14: Normal disomic pattern
- All informative markers show expected 1:1 or single allele patterns

Chromosome 15: Normal disomic pattern
- All informative markers show expected 1:1 or single allele patterns

Chromosome 18: Normal disomic pattern
- All informative markers show expected 1:1 or single allele patterns

Chromosome 21: Normal disomic pattern
- All informative markers show expected 1:1 or single allele patterns

Chromosome 22: Normal disomic pattern
- All informative markers show expected 1:1 or single allele patterns

Triploidy Assessment: No evidence of triploidy
- Diallelic and triallelic marker patterns inconsistent with triploidy

INTERPRETATION
QF-PCR analysis reveals two significant chromosomal abnormalities:
1. Trisomy 16 - confirmed by multiple informative markers
2. Monosomy X (Turner syndrome, 45,X) - single X chromosome with absence of Y chromosome

These chromosomal abnormalities are likely the cause of fetal loss. Trisomy 16 is the most common autosomal trisomy in spontaneous abortions but is incompatible with live birth. The combination with monosomy X represents a complex aneuploid karyotype. These findings are consistent with sporadic aneuploidy, which typically occurs as a random event during meiosis.

TEST LIMITATIONS
- QF-PCR detects aneuploidy only for the chromosomes tested
- Structural chromosomal abnormalities cannot be detected
- Low-level mosaicism (<20%) may not be detected
- Maternal cell contamination cannot be completely excluded
- This test does not detect balanced chromosomal rearrangements

RECOMMENDATIONS
1. Parental chromosomal testing (karyotype analysis) is recommended to exclude potential chromosome rearrangements involving chromosomes 16 or X
2. Genetic counseling is recommended to discuss:
   - The implications of these findings
   - Recurrence risks for future pregnancies
   - Prenatal testing options for subsequent pregnancies
3. If parental karyotypes are normal, the recurrence risk for sporadic aneuploidy is low (approximately 1%)

Reported by: [redacted name], PhD, FACMG
Laboratory Director: [redacted name], MD, PhD
